test_title: SSC Selection Post 2024 (Higher Secondary Level) Official Paper (Held On: 21 Jun, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements.

**Statements: **

I. All tables are charts.

II. Some charts are graphs.

III. Some graphs are pies.

**Conclusions:**

I. No table is a graph.

II. Some pies are charts.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow

solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d3d86d2fd2dea2c9eaf9ae87aef0e703bbf80e53ab20c718f297a0a0dd583059.png] 

Conclusions:

I. No table is a graph → Does not follow (As all tables are charts and some charts are graphs. As no direct relation is given between table and pies, therefore it is false.)

II. Some pies are charts → Does not follow (Because no relationship is given between pies and charts so it may be possible, but not defined.)

∴ Here, Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follow.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Neither conclusion I nor II follows"
